sources.root_cause_summary: Missing lowercasing of domain strings before PSL comparison bypasses public suffix check

summary: Cookie domain PSL verification calls `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()` without lowercasing the domain arguments first. Since PSL entries are lowercase and libpsl comparison is case-sensitive, a mixed-case cookie domain (e.g., "co.UK") bypasses the public suffix check, allowing a "super cookie" that leaks to all domains under the same TLD.

unsafe: Calling `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()` with domain strings that may contain uppercase characters without prior lowercasing, allowing mixed-case domains (e.g., "co.UK", "example.AT") to bypass the case-sensitive PSL comparison.
A wrapper function that directly delegates to `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()` without normalizing case on either the host domain or cookie domain arguments.
Passing a mixed-case cookie domain attribute alongside a lowercase host domain to the PSL check function, where the case mismatch defeats the public suffix restriction.
safe: Domain strings are lowercased via `Curl_strntolower()` (or equivalent) before being passed to `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()`, ensuring case-insensitive matching against the lowercase PSL entries.
Both the host domain and cookie domain are normalized to lowercase in local buffers before the PSL comparison call, so mixed-case cookie domains cannot bypass the public suffix check.
A case-insensitive comparison or normalization wrapper is interposed between the domain sources and the `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()` call.

anchors.behavior: Calling `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable()` with a PSL context pointer and two domain string arguments (host domain and cookie domain) to check cookie domain acceptability against the Public Suffix List.
anchors.inspect_hint: Check whether the domain arguments are lowercased before being passed to this function. Missing lowercasing means mixed-case domains (e.g., 'co.UK') bypass the case-sensitive PSL comparison, allowing cookie injection across origin boundaries.
